scope: Online adaptation, expert aggregation, meta-learning and continual portfolio learning; not the Relative Strength Index indicator, and not autonomous recursive researcher modification.
new_contribution: The earlier report emphasizes researcher evolution. These sources address the separate question of adapting a deployed investment rule to nonstationary observations, with its update rule fixed and testable.
work_performed: Primary-source literature inspection only. No new backtest, package installation, network market-data refresh, or changes to existing files.

papers.title: SAOFTRL: A Novel Adaptive Algorithmic Framework for Enhancing Online Portfolio Selection
papers.publication: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 72, 5291–5305; published 2024-11-11
papers.read_coverage: Author-hosted PDF indexed sections: Algorithm 1, assumptions, Theorems 1–2, SCA approximation, Section V and Section VI-A. Direct PDF opening repeatedly timed out; not represented as a successful full-PDF download.
papers.verified_summary: Geometric covering intervals maintain O(log t) active OFTRL portfolios, aggregated by CBCE weights. Optimistic gradients and regularization stabilize short-window estimates. Under bounded gradients/domain, the underlying OFTRL bound is O(N log(Q_T + log T)); this is not the complete strongly-adaptive meta bound. Section V relates the method to shrinkage mean–variance estimation and adaptive lookbacks. Experiments sample 80 one-year, 40-asset datasets per S&P500/NASDAQ100 list from 2010-01-01 through 2023-01-01.
papers.transaction_cost_evidence: No verified transaction-cost sensitivity or net-profit guarantee was located in the inspected primary passages; do not claim that one exists.
papers.official_code_status: No paper-specific author code repository verified from the paper, author pages and targeted search. This means unverified, not proof of nonexistence.
papers.assessment: Strong mechanism reference for multiple learning horizons; deployment evidence remains incomplete. BCRP-relative regret cannot imply positive absolute returns or preservation after arbitrary cost penalties.

papers.title: Adaptive Robust Online Portfolio Selection
papers.publication: European Journal of Operational Research 321(1), 214–230, 2025-02-16; accessible author preprint submitted 2022-06-02
papers.read_coverage: Publisher publication record plus author preprint Sections 3–5, Tables 1–2/9 and Appendix E. Preprint numerical details are not silently equated with an unseen final typeset revision.
papers.verified_summary: Ellipsoidal robust optimization explicitly penalizes trading. Parameter experts are updated sequentially. The selection-of-best scheme uses an incumbent-relative performance band and an indifference zone; another scheme averages top-K robustness parameters. Six legacy datasets and three additional US/HK/China stock datasets are tested. Additional datasets end 2021-08-30: SP500-21 starts 2016-01-04; HSI starts 2012-01-03; CSI starts 2012-01-04. Preprint costs include 0.2% and 0.5%. Results are not universally superior: on CSI at 0.2%, UBAH wealth 2.7323 exceeds RELP-Adap-1 2.0788 and RELP-Adap-2 0.5751.
papers.official_code_status: No author implementation verified; the paper references the general OLPS toolbox, which is not evidence that this method itself is implemented there.
papers.assessment: Most directly useful cost-aware adaptation mechanism here. The 2025 publication date does not mean a 2025-market test; cumulative-wealth expert selection can still lag or chase risk.

papers.title: Meta-Learning the Optimal Mixture of Strategies for Online Portfolio Selection
papers.publication: arXiv:2505.03659v1, 2025-05-06; no independently verified journal acceptance in this inspection
papers.read_coverage: Full HTML, especially Sections 3.1–3.2, Algorithm 1, Section 4 and Tables 3–7.
papers.verified_summary: Clusters historical strategy-return paths, selects four diverse candidate policies, and uses MAML to initialize quickly adaptable mixture weights. Training occurs across short tasks; online weights use preceding strategy returns. The cost model approximates proportional turnover against drifted previous asset weights; buy/sell rate is 0.0005. Six daily legacy datasets are used; single-market split is first 75% versus last 25%. Cross-market training uses NYSE(O), NYSE(N), DJIA and SP500; testing uses TSE/MSCI. Therefore the abstract's high-frequency suitability is not a high-frequency execution experiment. Table 4 reports DJIA Sharpe 208.71; metric scaling/implementation needs independent verification before comparison.
papers.experiment_dates: Paper Table 3 supplies counts, not calendar ranges. The named datasets are legacy OLPS datasets, not a verified 2025 trading sample.
papers.official_code_status: No author method code verified. The linked GitHub repository is the source OLPS toolbox/data, not LMPS implementation.
papers.assessment: Useful strategy-level representation and diversity idea, but return magnitudes, cost approximation, calendar transfer and reproducibility make this a research reference rather than a ready allocator.

papers.title: Regime-Adaptive Continual Learning for Portfolio Management
papers.publication: arXiv:2606.00143v1 submitted 2026-05-29; title/authors independently verified in official KDD 2026 paper list
papers.read_coverage: Full HTML: Sections 4–5, Algorithm 2, Appendix B, plus official conference list and author repository README.
papers.verified_summary: CUSUM regime detection triggers adaptation on completed segments. A frozen base actor plus stored parameter-difference vectors and a learned gate reuse regimes; merge/discard operations limit the library. Training is 2008-05-01–2020-04-30; evaluation is 2020-05-01–2025-04-29 over five datasets including seven commodity ETFs. Main experiments use 10 seeds, 10bp costs; NAS100 appendix adds 5/10bp stress. The paper explicitly retains continuously listed/data-available constituents over the whole period, creating survivorship concerns. NAS100 reports cumulative return 164.89%, Sharpe 1.14, MDD 23.86%; this is a historical result, not a live or A-share ETF finding.
papers.official_code_status: Verified author repository exists, but explicitly offers a minimum runnable implementation, not full reproduction; training steps are substantially reduced and missing VIX/turbulence invokes fallback features.
papers.assessment: Strongest recent direct analogue for regime-library reuse, but it mixes neural-network parameters, not arbitrary rule-based ETF strategy code. No universal regret or future-profit guarantee follows.

papers.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning
papers.read_coverage: Main paper Sections 1–4 and supplement theorem proof excerpts.
papers.verified_summary: A reduction combines interval-started learners to compete on every interval with that interval's best comparator, with logarithmic computational overhead. Theorem 1 includes both the base learner's interval regret and a square-root interval/meta overhead. Theorem 3 gives an impossibility result for the stated strong-adaptivity criterion under adversarial bandit-only feedback. This is a comparator-relative theorem under specified feedback/loss assumptions, not a financial profit experiment or a guarantee of instant regime recognition.
papers.assessment: Explains why retaining learners at several ages is principled, and why a claimed guarantee must state comparator, interval length, feedback assumptions and costs.

recommended_order: First: a small, frozen set of economically different strategy experts and a cost-aware, slowly changing allocation rule. Compare against static equal weighting and the frozen incumbent.
Second: several fixed learning ages / restart schedules, inspired by strongly adaptive learning, to avoid choosing one recent window after seeing its result.
Third: regime-conditioned expert reuse, with trigger timing and all post-trigger learning delays explicit. Preserve old regime experts instead of blindly overwriting them.
Later: MAML or neural parameter-vector continual learning only if simpler mixture controls have established a reproducible benefit.
minimum_state_contract: Expert holdings, lock periods and units evolve continuously even when allocation is zero; an expert must not receive a free favorable restart.
At decision t, the allocator may use only feedback whose economic outcome was already observable before that decision; update after next-period realized returns.

Record current portfolio weights after market drift. Form the aggregate asset target from expert actions, then charge actual aggregate turnover, spreads and execution delay; weighted averages of individual expert net returns are not the same portfolio.
Keep learning-rate, forgetting/restart rules, expert admission, weight bounds and turnover budget inside the frozen candidate definition. Changing the updater is a new model version.
An expert introduced after deployment has a birth time and a distinct forward record. Retroactive good performance does not become contemporaneous evidence.
A change alarm can trigger diagnosis or lower risk. It does not by itself identify the replacement strategy or prove a regime label.
synthesis_our_inferences_not_paper_claim.regret_interpretation: For negative log-wealth loss, a regret bound R implies log(W_best/W_algorithm) <= R for its stated comparator/model. The comparator may itself lose money; R can be large over short intervals. Adding turnover penalties, stateful locks, changing expert pools or uncertain fills requires checking the theorem again, not retaining the old guarantee by analogy.
a_share_etf_boundaries: These papers mostly allocate continuously across many stocks. Applying them to 11 ETFs with discrete holdings, minimum lots, cash sleeves and lock states changes the action and cost model.

QDII asynchronous prices/NAV, ETF premium changes, actual quote availability and execution windows require local point-in-time evidence; none of the inspected papers validates this repository's 14:50 clock.
A small ETF pool offers limited independent regime episodes. Many near-identical parameter variants create redundant experts and can amplify noise rather than add useful diversity.
For this repository, observed legacy versions have often shared the same holdings. Expert diversity must be measured by actual action and net-return differences, not version labels.

Online allocation adapts a strategy state under a fixed learning law. It becomes recursive research improvement only if the research/learning law itself is modified and independently evaluated across generations.
what_would_falsify_the_proposal: Adaptive allocation fails to beat the same experts under static weights after aggregate execution costs.
Apparent benefit disappears when every expert uses only its birth-time-available data and continuous state.
Benefit concentrates in one crisis/rebound or depends on arbitrary update-day choice.
Weights become winner-take-all on a handful of observations, or regime triggers repeatedly reverse before costs can be recovered.

unresolved_checks: SAOFTRL direct PDF fetch failed; indexed author-PDF passages were inspected but full cost discussion could not be verified.
Adaptive Robust detailed tests refer to its accessible 2022 preprint; final EJOR full-text differences are not certified.
Meta-mixture has no verified author code and unusually large reported Sharpe values; no claim of implementation correctness is made.
